en: The Ritual Manual for Recitation and the Method of Offering according to the *Sūtra on the Merit of the Fundamental Vows of the Seven Buddhas, Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha-rāja*,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Śaraba, a śramaṇa of the Great Yuan, by Imperial Decree.
May this entire ground of mine be free of all rubble, gravel, sand, and impurities;

may it be as level and excellent as the palm of a hand. May it become a pure ground of lapis lazuli, adorned like the Land of Ultimate Bliss, with various jewels interspersed and covered everywhere by flowers.
Jewel trees and jewel ponds are all complete, All resound with the subtle and wondrous sound of the Great Dharma;
Born from supramundane roots of goodness, Accomplished by various kinds of exquisite jewels,
And endowed with immeasurable great radiance— May all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas dwell therein in peace.
Fundamentally free from coming and going, increase or decrease, and bodily form, Because of your perfect and subtle supreme vows,
you appear like the radiance of white light; To save the world, we pray that you descend upon this pure,
vast, and wondrous jewel throne, Your body entirely free from all obstacles.
Abiding in equality, may you remain forever; Please accept this great seat of profound peace.
Unwavering from the nature of the pure *dharmadhātu*, With great compassion, you observe all sentient beings;
Having perfected the wondrous conduct of Great Enlightenment, O Guide of the Three Times, please descend here.
For the sake of benefiting all sentient beings who suffer, you manifest your descent into the mire of the world;
yet you are not stained by the dust of the three realms of existence. Having fulfilled all vows, the Guide ascends the lotus throne;
O Honored One among Sattvas, you rescue and deliver those within the triple world.
May you grant your blessings to us through the threefold gathering of body, speech, and mind;
Abiding in the nature of great bliss and luminosity, out of compassion for us sentient beings,
May the clouds of your mercy spread throughout the ten directions, And may you let fall a rain of all the *siddhi* jewels.
In the world of Aparājita in the eastern direction, the Buddha named Śubhākīrti,
surrounded by an immeasurable host who have distanced themselves from afflictions and perfected their vows— For the benefit of the noble donor,
I pray that you descend from the eastern land adorned with exquisite jewels; O Ratnacandravijayaśrī, together with your immeasurable host.
To eliminate and dispel distraction and strife, for the benefit of the noble benefactors,
may you descend from the eastern realm of Pūrṇapradīpa. Golden-hued, jewel-light, surrounded by an immeasurable host,
extending longevity and bestowing prophecy at the time of death— for the benefit of the noble benefactors, may you descend.
In the world of Aśoka in the eastern quarter, Where the peerless Aśoka King and his immeasurable host have removed all suffering and eliminated karmic obstructions—
For the benefit of the noble donors, we pray that you descend from the eastern world-realm of Dharmadhvaja,
Where the Dharma-ocean’s Thunderous Voice and his immeasurable host reside.
Dispelling all obstacles and difficulties of wrong views, for the benefit of the noble donor,
please descend from the Eastern Land of the Jewel Ocean of Excellent Abiding.
From the Samādhi of the Pure Land of the Infinite Multitude Perfecting the Supreme Wisdom of the Dharma-Ocean, for the benefit of the noble donor, please descend.
In the pure eastern realm of Vaiḍūrya, The Bhaisajyaguru, Sun, and Moon, with all-encompassing radiance,
Possessing the marks and signs of perfection, have descended to subdue Māra; For the benefit of the noble donors,
may you, the Supreme Munis and Sugatas, Endowed with immeasurable merit and the power of all Buddhas, descend here.
Without abandoning the sublime practices and vows, for the sake of benefiting noble donors, please descend;
you who have severed delusions and karma with the sword of universal knowledge through the mastery of speech,
kindle the torch of Dharma and perfect our merit through the scriptures— therefore, O Noble Assembly, please descend.
Those who take refuge in you shall be liberated from the suffering of illness;
may you fulfill the unsurpassed aspirations of the Muni to utterly purify the agonizing torments at the time of death. For our benefit, we pray that you descend;
O Great Brahmā, Śakra, and all Dharma protectors, grant us mastery over the remedies for sensual desires.
The lay practitioners and others entreat the assembly: for the sake of benefiting sentient beings, please descend!
O Son of the Mind of the Sovereign of Secrets, who tames both hatred and love;
you whose excellent vows are perfected like those of the seven Buddhas; and who possess great supernatural power—please descend!
May your wondrous spiritual power protect these merits;
As the Lord of the Family, honored among those who overcome all fears, To the assembly of Kumbhīra generals, we offer this invocation: For the sake of benefiting sentient beings, please descend;
O Great Compassionate One, do not fail your original vow; Think with loving-kindness upon all beings, O Eight Tathāgatas.
With sincere faith, I now establish this maṇḍala; together with the great assembly, I pray that all the Sugatas, Bhagavans, will descend.
Out of great compassion, please look upon us with pity;
we too possess a portion of merit. I entreat you: please remain seated upon this precious throne.

By the power of the World-Honored One’s supernormal knowledges and majestic virtue, out of compassion for us sentient beings, may the World-Honored One, with great kindness, deign to descend. We entreat you:
please remain upon this seat. While we present these offerings, may you dwell peacefully within this sacred precinct.
Accepting the offerings of argha and so forth, may you likewise fulfill our aspirations;
just as when the Tathāgata descended into birth, all the devas performed his ablution,
so too do I bathe you with pure, celestial, and wondrous waters.
The nature of true wisdom is primordially pure; Free from the afflictions of subject-object grasping, it purifies the habitual stains of sentient beings.
I bathe the hands and feet of the assembly of noble ones, And provide the refreshing water of Dharma to satisfy all sentient beings afflicted by the thirst of their own afflictions.
Purify all our defilements; we offer this water from the vessel, pray accept it.
Lions, elephant kings, and noble steeds, vajras, maṇi-jewels, suns, moons, and disks— Upon these stainless and pure lotus seats, may you abide in the state of non-abiding.
The intrinsic nature of all phenomena is fundamentally pure;
though powerless against all defiling characteristics, it accords with the world through the Dharma of reverence.
Abiding upon the lotus seat of non-attachment, its nature of great compassion does not enter parinirvāṇa, for it does not abandon afflictions yet remains untainted by them.
Inherently unattached and fundamentally pure, Please abide upon the seat of the pure lotus;
For all sentient beings oppressed by the poisons of affliction, Your great compassion is like nectar that can purify them.
Because of your perfect and sublime supreme vows, I prostrate and pay homage to the assembly of Sugatas.
Seeing those sentient beings oppressed by afflictions, karma, and suffering,
I arouse great compassion for them and make vast vows to eliminate their afflictions. I pay homage to the assembly of the seven noble Buddhas,
who are replete with the jewels of manifold virtues and possess pure wisdom-bodies adorned with sublime marks.
To those whose bodies are golden, honored by humans and devas, To the Tathāgata, the God among Gods,
whose nature is the pure and tranquil Dharmadhātu, To the Tathāgatas who are like the sovereign maṇi-jewel,
manifesting emanated bodies throughout the worlds of the ten directions— I offer worship, praise, and prostrate with reverence.
The Jewel of the Supreme Triple Gem, whose merit is a treasure; Through reverent faith, inconceivable blessings are obtained.
O Honored One who can save all *sattvas*, To the Triple Gem worthy of offerings, I pay homage.
To the World-Honored One of great compassion and wondrous adornment, The Honored One of Right Universal Knowledge, the Great Guide.
I pay homage to the Tathāgatas, who can bestow merit and wisdom like a great ocean;
I pay homage to the sublime Dharma of tranquility, which is pure by nature, free from all desires,
And which enables liberation from the evil realms through its single flavor of profound and wondrous principle.
Realizing the path of liberation and demonstrating liberation, One who upholds the *śīla* should be honored with reverence;
Born from merit, the supreme field of blessings, The most venerable among all assemblies—to you I pay homage.
For those who delight in elaboration, the extensive praise of the Three Jewels is as found in other texts.
The Buddha’s body is adorned with all manner of ornaments, Exceedingly graced by the marks and signs of a Great Being;
To eliminate defilements and fulfill his vows,
I therefore offer this maṇḍala born of its own causal nature, Along with all the sublime celestial argha water.
I offer to the ocean-like assembly of Sugatas; for the benefit of sentient beings, please accept this.
Arising from the nature of causes and conditions, I offer all varieties of sublime celestial flowers to the ocean-like assembly of Sugatas;
for the benefit of sentient beings, please accept them.
All various sublime celestial incenses produced from the nature of causes and conditions, I offer to the ocean-like assembly of the Sugatas;
for the benefit of sentient beings, may you graciously accept them.
All various sublime celestial lamps produced from the nature of causes and conditions...
I offer to the ocean-like assembly of Sugatas; for the benefit of sentient beings, please accept this.
Arising from the nature of causes and conditions, I offer all varieties of sublime celestial waters to the ocean-like assembly of Sugatas;
for the benefit of sentient beings, please accept them.
I offer all varieties of divine, exquisite foods produced from the nature of causes and conditions to the ocean-like assembly of Sugatas;
for the benefit of sentient beings, may you graciously accept them.
I offer all varieties of divine, exquisite delights produced from the nature of causes and conditions.

I offer to the ocean-like assembly of Sugatas garments of various celestial wondrous fabrics, produced from the nature of causes and conditions; for the benefit of sentient beings, may you graciously accept them.
I offer to the ocean-like assembly of Sugatas all manner of divine and exquisite robes; for the benefit of sentient beings, may you graciously accept them.
All manner of various offering implements, And all the worldly offerings, I present to the ocean-like assembly of Sugatas;
For the benefit of sentient beings, may you graciously accept them.
All manner of various sublime medicines, To eliminate all suffering of illness, [I offer].
I offer this to the ocean-like assembly of Sugatas; for the benefit of the noble patrons, may you graciously accept it.
Before the ocean-like assemblies of the seven Tathāgatas, I now offer this great jewel wheel;
may it sever the suffering of saṃsāra within the three realms of existence and turn the unsurpassed, wondrous Wheel of Dharma.
Before the ocean-like assembly of the seven Tathāgatas, I now offer this maṇi jewel;
may the suffering of poverty and deprivation be severed, and may all necessities for enjoyment be abundantly fulfilled.
Before the ocean-like assembly of the seven Tathāgatas, I now offer this precious jewel of a beautiful woman.
Dispelling the profound darkness of ignorance, may you realize the Mother Prajñāpāramitā and proceed before the ocean-like assembly of the seven Tathāgatas. I now offer this Jewel of a Minister,
who thoroughly masters the subtle wisdom of the Three Vehicles and has brought all meritorious qualities to ultimate perfection.
Before the ocean-like assembly of the seven Tathāgatas, I now offer this precious horse;
may it enable me to transcend the three realms of existence and attain divine feet, swiftly proceeding to all Buddha-fields.
Before the ocean-like assembly of the seven Tathāgatas, I now offer this precious elephant.
Having severed evil views and relied upon the Mahāyāna, may they swiftly proceed to the city of liberation and omniscience.
Before the ocean-like assembly of the seven Tathāgatas, I now offer this General Jewel;
may it subdue the enemies of the afflictions and realize the supreme principle of freedom from pride.
All the evil karmas I have created in the past, Arising from beginningless greed, hatred, and delusion,
Produced by my body, speech, and mind— I now repent them all.
To all sentient beings throughout the ten directions, And to those of the two vehicles, both with and without further training,
I rejoice in all the merits of all Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas.
To all the Lamps of the World throughout the ten directions who have first attained enlightenment,
I now entreat you all to turn the unsurpassed, wondrous wheel of Dharma.
All Buddhas desire to manifest *nirvāṇa*; I entreat them all with sincere devotion:
I pray that you remain for as many eons as there are motes of dust in a world-system, To bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings.
Whatever merit is gained from prostrations, praises, and offerings, I dedicate it to requesting the Buddhas to remain in the world and turn the wheel of Dharma.
I rejoice in and repent for all roots of goodness, dedicating them toward sentient beings and the path of the Buddha.
Regarding all the merits described in the sutras, for the benefit of the noble donors and all living beings,
I pray that the assembly of the eight Great Tathāgatas will swiftly grant their empowerment and bring this to fulfillment.
The flowers of sublime marks have blossomed in purity; The fruits of secondary characteristics adorn his upright body.

To see, hear, or remember him brings auspiciousness; I pay homage to the Buddha of Excellent Renown, whose great person is adorned with the marks and signs, And who possesses a heart of great, rare compassion.
The perfect voice pervades worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges; I offer to the Buddha King of Good Renown.
With water of pure merit, inexhaustible like the waters of the Gaṅgā, I present this offering to the Buddha King of Good Renown; May you, out of compassion, graciously accept it.
With the fragrant vapors of *pāṭala*, *mandārava*, and *utpala* flowers,
I offer to the Tathāgata of Excellent Renown; may you, out of compassion,
graciously accept these exquisite forests of incense and pleasing celestial perfumes that pervade everywhere with their rich fragrance.

I offer this lamp of wondrous light, auspicious and endowed with excellence, which can dispel the deep darkness of ignorance, to the Tathāgata Suviśruta; I pray that out of your compassion you will graciously accept it.
I offer this lamp of wondrous light, auspicious and endowed with excellence, which can dispel the deep darkness of ignorance, to the Tathāgata Suviśruta;
I pray that out of your compassion you will graciously accept it.
With saffron, sandalwood, and other blended substances, as well as various kinds of fragrant waters for anointing, I offer them to the Tathāgata of Excellent Renown;
may you, out of compassion, graciously accept them.
With all kinds of medicinal essences that are pleasing to the senses, and with rare delicacies and exquisite foods of supreme flavor—
I offer to the Tathāgata Bhadraśrī; may you, out of compassion, graciously accept all these lutes, musical instruments, and every other subtle and exquisite sound offered to the Tathāgata Bhadraśrī;
may you, out of compassion, graciously accept them.
All manner of various wondrous medicines, offered to remove all suffering of illness before the ocean-like assembly of Sugatas—
may you accept these for the benefit of the noble patrons;
likewise, may you accept these various articles of offering and all worldly offerings.
Before the ocean-like assembly of Sugatas, for the benefit of the noble patrons, I pray that you accept this offering.
All the evil karma I have previously created— arising from body, speech, and mind through beginningless greed, hatred, and delusion— I now confess it all.
I rejoice in all the merit of all sentient beings throughout the ten directions, of those in the two vehicles—
both those still training and those beyond training— and of all Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas.
I rejoice in all the merit of the lamps of the world throughout the ten directions, who first achieved the realization of Bodhi.
I now exhort all [the Buddhas] to turn the unsurpassed, wondrous wheel of Dharma;
If the Buddhas wish to manifest parinirvāṇa, I entreat them all with sincere resolve:
"May you remain for as many eons as there are atoms in a buddha-field, Bringing benefit and happiness to all sentient beings."
All merit from prostrating, praising, and making offerings, Requesting the Buddhas to remain in the world and turn the wheel of Dharma,
Rejoicing in, confessing, and all roots of goodness— I dedicate them to sentient beings and the path of the Buddha,
That the Guide may always act as our refuge And bring benefit to all living beings.
Who has fully realized all matters of peace and happiness, May he grant constant auspiciousness and tranquility;
To the one adorned with the exquisite lotus of the jewel-moon, Who thoroughly knows all knowable phenomena,
Whose body is as vast as the great ocean— I pay homage to Ratnacandraprajñābhūṣaṇa.
Your wondrous jewel-like body is pure, like moonlight that dispels suffering and distress;
it is unstained, like a lotus. To you, whose most exquisite body is so majestic and sublime, I offer this pure, stainless, and most excellent *argha* water.

I offer these various exquisite jewel flowers, grown from both water and land, before the Tathāgata King of Light and Sound; for the sake of benefiting sentient beings, may you graciously accept them.
For the sake of benefiting sentient beings, may you graciously accept them.
All the various exquisite celestial incenses found throughout all worlds in the ten directions,
I offer before the Tathāgata Prabhāsvara; may he accept them for the benefit of sentient beings,
as they are able to dispel the darkness of all ignorance, just like the sun, the moon, and lamps.
I offer before the Tathāgata Prabhāsvara all pleasing unguents, May you accept them for the sake of benefiting sentient beings;
May they remove all stains of transgressing the precepts.
I offer before the Tathāgata Prabhāsvara all pleasing unguents, May you accept them for the sake of benefiting sentient beings.
All manner of exquisite celestial foods throughout all worlds in the ten directions are offered before the Tathāgata Prabhāsvara;
for the sake of benefiting sentient beings, may you graciously accept them.
May the supreme sound of mani-jewel bells and various subtle, wonderful musical performances likewise be accepted.
I offer before the Tathāgata Prabhāsvara all manner of sublime medicines, for the sake of benefiting sentient beings;

may you accept them out of compassion. I offer before the Tathāgata Prabhāsvara [these offerings] to eliminate all suffering of illness; for the sake of benefiting sentient beings, may you accept them.
With these various kinds of offerings and all the worldly offerings presented before the Tathāgata Ābhāsvara, for the benefit of the noble donors, may you accept them from me.
All the evil karma I have previously created arose from beginningless greed, hatred, and delusion.
I now confess all that has arisen from my body, speech, and mind.
I rejoice in all the merits of every sentient being throughout the ten directions, of those on the two vehicles—
both those still training and those beyond training— and of all Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas.
I now exhort all those who are lamps for the worlds throughout the ten directions, the first to achieve enlightenment;
I beseech them all to turn the unsurpassed, wondrous wheel of Dharma.
And when the Buddhas wish to manifest their entry into nirvana, I entreat them all with sincere resolve.
I only pray that you will dwell for as many eons as there are atoms in a buddha-field, Bringing benefit and happiness to all sentient beings.
Whatever merit there is from prostrating, praising, and making offerings, From requesting the Buddha to remain in the world and turn the wheel of Dharma,
And from rejoicing, repenting, and all roots of goodness— I dedicate this to all sentient beings and to the path of Buddhahood.
Bhagavān, Greatly Compassionate Savior, Out of pity for all sentient beings as if they were your only child,
please grant your protection. May you always remain auspicious and at peace,
with a body like the true golden hue of Jambū, And with majestic radiance surpassing that of a thousand suns.
I pay homage to the stainless Radiant Banner, whose golden jewel-light illuminates my praise;
his pure body is like Jambu-river gold, with exquisite marks, majestic and uniquely stainless.
With golden jewel-light that is utterly translucent, I make offerings to the Teacher’s wondrously colored body.
Pure, stainless, and pleasing, this most excellent water of merit from the gods is offered to the Tathāgata Golden Light;
for the sake of benefiting sentient beings, may you graciously accept it.
Likewise, these most excellent flowers, incense, lamps, unguents, and foods are offered.
And with various musical instruments and articles of worship, I offer all kinds of wondrous medicinal herbs to the Tathāgata Suvarṇaprabhāsa;
To eliminate all suffering from illness, I offer them to the Tathāgata Suvarṇaprabhāsa;
For the benefit of sentient beings, I pray that you will graciously accept them.
With these various kinds of offerings and all the worldly offerings presented to the Tathāgata Golden Light,
for the benefit of the noble donor, may you graciously accept them.
All the evil karma I have created in the past arises entirely from beginningless greed, hatred, and delusion.
I now repent of all that has arisen from my body, speech, and mind.
I rejoice in all the merits of all sentient beings throughout the ten directions, Of those on the two vehicles—
both those still training and those beyond training— And of all the Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas.
I now exhort all the lamps of the world throughout the ten directions, those who first attained enlightenment,
to turn the unsurpassed, wondrous wheel of Dharma;
and whenever the Buddhas wish to manifest parinirvāṇa, I entreat them all with sincere devotion.
I pray that you remain for as many eons as there are motes of dust in a world-system, To bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings.
Whatever merit there is in prostrating, praising, and making offerings, In requesting the Buddha to remain in the world and turn the wheel of Dharma,
In rejoicing in others' virtue, repenting one's own faults, and cultivating roots of goodness— I dedicate this to all sentient beings and to the path of Buddhahood.
For all those submerged in the ocean of birth and death, may you act as their refuge and provide for them as a land and its kin;
may you cause them to be ever auspicious and at peace,
so that they may ultimately attain nirvāṇa and sublime bliss, and may you be able to eliminate all the sufferings and hardships of sentient beings.
I pay homage and praise the Auspicious King who rescues and protects the six realms of existence, the most supreme one free from sorrow;
He who crosses the ocean of the three worlds to the further shore, attaining ultimate nirvāṇa and the wondrous bliss, abiding in the most sublime body of the dharmadhātu;
The Honored One who has renounced the three worlds and is worthy of offerings.
The Sugata’s supreme state is free from sorrow;
it is suffused with the fragrances of *pāṭala*, *māndārava*, and *utpala* flowers.
There are all manner of lovely and exquisite flower garlands, the finest incense, and pleasing perfumes—such vast oceans of clouds of various scents.
Along with various kinds of exquisite food and drink, celestial delicacies, and manifold offerings of adornments;
numerous golden lotuses, mani-jewel lamps, and ritual implements;
the ground strewn with subtle fragrances and anointed with ointments; and scattered everywhere are various flowers that gladden the mind.
Supreme and wondrous palaces adorned with various jewels, And the exquisite sounds of chanting and praise;
Brilliantly radiant necklaces of precious gems— Such immeasurable ornaments,
each pervading the entirety of space, Are offered to King Aśokaśrī.
A supreme and wondrous parasol with a handle made entirely of jewels, Completely covered by nets of various precious garlands,
held upright and perfectly full, most lovely to behold;
I offer all kinds of wondrous medicinal herbs belonging to the King of Sorrowless Auspiciousness, To eliminate all sufferings of disease.
I offer these various articles of worship And all worldly offerings to King Aśokaśrī; For the benefit of sentient beings, I pray you accept them.
I offer these to King Aśokaśrī; For the benefit of the noble donor, I pray you accept them.
All the evil karmas I have created in the past, Arising from beginningless greed, hatred, and delusion,
Produced by my body, speech, and mind— I now confess them all.
To all sentient beings throughout the ten directions, And those of the two vehicles, both with and without training.
I rejoice in all the merits of all Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas.
To all the Lamps of the World throughout the ten directions, Who first attained the realization of Bodhi,
I now entreat them all To turn the supreme and wondrous Wheel of Dharma.
If the Buddhas wish to manifest parinirvāṇa, I shall with sincere devotion entreat them:
"May you remain for as many eons as there are motes of dust in a buddha-field, for the benefit and happiness of all sentient beings.
Whatever merit is gained from prostrations, praise, and offerings, and through this request for the Buddhas to remain in the world and turn the wheel of Dharma—
Rejoicing in and repenting of all roots of goodness, I dedicate them to sentient beings and the path of the Buddha.
May I realize the pure Dharma-body before me— Pure, non-illusory, and free from inversion;
may this pure speech bring about purification. May all be auspicious and ever peaceful.
With a profound and wondrous voice like the tide, you resound the great Dharma sound to crush heterodox arguments;
able to eliminate the various sufferings of affliction, I pay homage to you, the thunderous voice of the Dharma-ocean.
Your Dharma-sound vibrates throughout the three thousandfold world-system, employing sixty kinds of tones to transform all living beings.
The wondrous meaning is as profound as the great ocean; I offer to the World-Honored One the most exquisite jewel-canopy of sublime sound, which completely covers the realm of space.
Clouds of universal jewel-garlands and necklaces, with fragrant waters as pleasing as the great ocean, Shower down a rain of *argha* and nectar.
Universally pervading clouds of exquisite fragrant incense, surpassing the light of the sun, moon, lamps, and candles;
scattered infinite mani-flowers, various foods of a hundred flavors and the finest quality,
as well as immeasurable music and the like— these fill the entire realm of space as an offering.
Such are these most excellent requisites, including the exquisite māndārava flowers found throughout the realm of Tuṣita Heaven, all the most wonderful ornaments of the gods,
every unsurpassed offering, and those manifested by my own pure mind.
Before this holy assembly of the Tathāgata, with sincere devotion and reverence, I offer all manner of wondrous medicines to eliminate every suffering of illness.
I present these to the Buddha Dharma-sāgara-nirghoṣa; for the benefit of the noble donor, I pray that you will accept them.
With these various articles of offering thus planted, and all the worldly offerings presented to the Buddha Dharma-sāgara-ghoṣa,
for the benefit of the noble donor, I pray that you accept them.
All the evil karma I have created in the past arises entirely from beginningless greed, hatred, and delusion.
I now confess all that has arisen from my body, speech, and mind.
I rejoice in all the merits of every sentient being throughout the ten directions, of those on the two vehicles—
both those still training and those beyond training— and of all Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas.
I now exhort all those who are lamps for the worlds throughout the ten directions, those who have first attained perfect enlightenment,
to turn the unsurpassed, wondrous wheel of Dharma;
and whenever the Buddhas wish to manifest their parinirvāṇa, I entreat them all with sincere resolve.
I only pray that you will dwell for as many eons as there are atoms in a buddha-field, Bringing benefit and happiness to all sentient beings.
Whatever merit there is in prostrating, praising, and making offerings, In requesting the Buddha to remain in the world and turn the wheel of Dharma,
In rejoicing, repenting, and all roots of goodness— I dedicate this to all sentient beings and to the path of Buddhahood.
At the time of the Great Hero’s birth, may all magnificent events be accomplished;
may every siddhi be fully realized. May there be constant auspiciousness and peace through the unfathomable great Dharma-wisdom, sporting within the pure realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu).
I pay homage to you who have thoroughly realized all knowable phenomena, Who sport with supernatural powers, and have perfectly attained subtle and wondrous superknowledges;
To you who protect all sentient beings with the Dharma-body, And who transform the multitudes through the play of supreme wisdom; I offer worship to your subtle and wondrous self-nature body.
All the sublime divine *argha* water produced from the nature of causes and conditions, I offer to the Buddha who sports in supernatural powers;
for the benefit of the noble patrons, may you graciously accept it.
All the various kinds of sublime divine flowers produced from the nature of causes and conditions—
I offer divine, exquisite incenses of every variety, born of the nature of causes and conditions, to the Buddha Līlā-vikrīḍita; for the benefit of the noble donor, may you graciously accept them.
I offer divine, exquisite incenses of every variety, born of the nature of causes and conditions, to the Buddha Līlā-vikrīḍita;
for the benefit of the noble donor, may you graciously accept them.
All various sublime celestial lamps produced from the nature of causes and conditions, I offer to the Buddha who sports in supernatural powers;
for the benefit of the noble donor, may you graciously accept them.
All various sublime celestial waters produced from the nature of causes and conditions...
I offer to the Buddha Līlā-vikrīḍita; for the benefit of the noble donor, may you graciously accept this.
Arising from the nature of causes and conditions, I offer all manner of sublime celestial foods to the Buddha Līlā-vikrīḍita;
for the benefit of the noble donor, may you graciously accept them.
Born from the nature of causes and conditions,
I offer all these various sublime celestial medicines to the Buddha who sports with supernatural powers; for the benefit of the noble donors,
may you accept all these various sublime medicines to eliminate all suffering of illness.
I offer these various articles of worship, as well as all worldly offerings, to the Buddha of Playful Supernatural Powers;

for the benefit of the noble donor, may you graciously accept them. I offer these various articles of worship, as well as all worldly offerings, to the Buddha of Playful Supernatural Powers; for the benefit of the noble donor, may you graciously accept them.
All the evil karmas I have created in the past, Arising from beginningless greed, hatred, and delusion,
Produced by my body, speech, and mind— I now repent them all.
To all sentient beings throughout the ten directions, And those of the two vehicles, both with and without further training,
I rejoice in all the merits of all Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas.
To all the Lamps of the World throughout the ten directions, who first attained perfect enlightenment,
I now entreat you all to turn the supreme, wondrous Wheel of Dharma.
Whenever the Buddhas wish to manifest parinirvāṇa, I shall with sincere resolve entreat them:
"May you remain for as many eons as there are atoms in a buddha-field, for the benefit and happiness of all sentient beings.
Whatever merit is gained from prostrations, praises, and offerings, and through this request for the Buddhas to remain in the world and turn the wheel of Dharma—
I rejoice in and repent for all roots of virtue, dedicating them toward sentient beings and the path of the Buddha.
At the time of each initial descent into birth, the mountains, forests, and great earth all tremble;
may all sentient beings give rise to joy, and may they always abide in auspiciousness and peace.
To the Honored One, Superior Medicine, who can eliminate the suffering of illness, Whose body is like lapis lazuli, radiant and translucent,
shining with light such that those touched by it attain liberation— To the Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyarāja, I pay homage;
Like the sun’s light dispelling darkness, And like the moonlight dispelling distress.
Able to cure the suffering of sentient beings' three poisons, I worship Bhaisajyaguru-vaidūrya-prabha as if he were the Great King of Physicians in the world;
Able to eliminate the diseases of afflictions and distress like the pure vaidūrya jewel,
his body of wisdom— I worship him who can remove the suffering of the three poisons.
All subtle *argha* water, And all the waters of merit in the world, I offer to the Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguru-prabha;

For the benefit of sentient beings, I pray you accept them. All varieties of celestial wondrous flowers, And all the wondrous flowers of the world, I offer to the Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguru-prabha; For the benefit of sentient beings, I pray you accept them.

I offer various kinds of exquisite celestial incense, And all manner of wonderful worldly incenses, To the Tathāgata Bhaisajyaguru-rāja; For the benefit of sentient beings, may you graciously accept them.
I offer various kinds of exquisite celestial incense, And all manner of wonderful worldly incenses, To the Tathāgata Bhaisajyaguru-rāja;
For the benefit of sentient beings, may you graciously accept them.
All manner of sublime celestial lamps And all the various exquisite lamps of the world, I offer to the Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguru-prabha;
For the benefit of sentient beings, may you graciously accept them.

All manner of sublime celestial ointments And all the various exquisite ointments of the world, I offer to the Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguru-prabha; For the benefit of sentient beings, may you graciously accept them.
I offer to the Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguru-prabha;
for the benefit of sentient beings, may you graciously accept all these various sublime celestial foods and all the exquisite foods of the world.
I offer to the Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguru-prabha; for the benefit of sentient beings, may you graciously accept them.
All manner of celestial delights, And all the various worldly pleasures, I offer to the Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguru-prabha;
For the benefit of sentient beings, may you graciously accept them.
All manner of various excellent medicines, To eliminate the suffering of illness for sentient beings.
I offer these various articles of worship, as well as all worldly offerings, to the Tathāgata Bhaisajyaguru-prabha; for the benefit of the noble donor, may you graciously accept them.
I offer these to the Buddha Bhaisajyaguru-vaidūryaprabha; for the benefit of the noble donor, may you graciously accept them.
All the evil karma I have created in the past, Arising from beginningless greed, hatred, and delusion,
Produced by my body, speech, and mind— I now confess it all.
To all sentient beings throughout the ten directions, And to those of the two vehicles, both with and without further training,
I rejoice in all the merits of all Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas.
To all the Lamps of the World throughout the ten directions, Who first attained the realization of Bodhi,
I now entreat them all to turn The unsurpassed, wondrous Wheel of Dharma.
Should any Buddhas wish to manifest nirvāṇa, I shall with all sincerity entreat them,
praying that they remain for as many eons as there are motes of dust in a buddha-field, to bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings.
May the merit of all my prostrations, praises, and offerings, and my entreaties for the Buddhas to remain in the world and turn the wheel of Dharma, [be dedicated to this end].
Rejoicing in and repenting of all roots of goodness, I dedicate them to sentient beings and the path of the Buddha.
Whenever I proceed toward Bodhi, may the great earth tremble in six ways, causing all the hosts of Māras to be filled with grief and distress; may all be auspicious and ever peaceful.
Born of the Śākya clan through the skillful means of great compassion, Subduing the hosts of invincible Māras,
his body as majestic as a mountain of gold; To the Dharma-King Śākyamuni, the Sugata,
the Honored Being of the Solar Lineage, The Protector of the Three Realms, the God among Gods, I pay homage and praise.
To the Immovable World-Honored One, the Śākya King, the most venerable and majestic Muni—
I offer all kinds of great and wondrous waters, as well as all the exquisite waters of the world;
I present them to the King Śākyamuni, For the benefit of the noble donor, I pray that you will graciously accept them.
All varieties of celestial wondrous flowers, And all the wondrous flowers of the world, I offer to King Śākyamuni;
For the benefit of the noble donor, may you graciously accept them.
All varieties of celestial wondrous incenses, And all the wondrous incenses of the world...
I offer these various sublime celestial lamps And all the exquisite lamps of the world To Śākyamuni, the King; For the benefit of the noble donor, May you graciously accept them.
I offer these various sublime celestial lamps And all the exquisite lamps of the world To Śākyamuni, the King;
For the benefit of the noble donor, May you graciously accept them.
All varieties of celestial sublime ointments, And all varieties of worldly sublime ointments, I offer to King Śākyamuni;
For the benefit of the noble patrons, may you graciously accept them.
All varieties of celestial sublime foods, And all varieties of worldly sublime foods, I offer to King Śākyamuni; For the benefit of the noble patrons, may you graciously accept them.
I offer to King Śākyamuni; for the benefit of the noble donor, may you graciously accept all manner of sublime celestial delights and all the exquisite joys of the world.
I offer to King Śākyamuni; for the benefit of the noble donor, may you graciously accept them.
All manner of various wondrous medicines, Offered to Śākyamuni Buddha to eliminate the suffering of all sentient beings’ illnesses—
For the benefit of the noble patrons, I pray you accept them; Thus,
these various articles of offering, As well as all worldly offerings.
I offer this to Śākyamuni Buddha; for the benefit of the noble patrons, may you graciously accept it.
All the various evil karmas I have previously created—arising from the body, speech, and mind through beginningless greed, hatred, and delusion—I now confess them all.
I rejoice in all the merits of all sentient beings throughout the ten directions, of those on the two vehicles—
both those still training and those beyond training— and of all Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas.
I rejoice in all the world-lamps throughout the ten directions who first achieved awakening.
I now exhort all [the Buddhas] to turn the unsurpassed, wondrous wheel of Dharma;
If any Buddhas wish to manifest parinirvāṇa, I shall exhort them all with sincere resolve:
"May you remain for as many eons as there are motes of dust in a world-system, Bringing benefit and happiness to all sentient beings."
May all merit from prostrations, praises, and offerings, The request for the Buddha to remain in the world and turn the wheel of Dharma,
Rejoicing, repentance, and all roots of goodness— Dedicate this to sentient beings and all paths.
When he first turned the Great Wheel of Dharma, He proclaimed the teachings on the Four Noble Truths.
The fame of the Muni increases ever more and more; May he grant auspiciousness and constant peace, Like space, tranquil and signless.
Having transcended defilement, he gives rise to all virtues;
He is the path of liberation that rescues and delivers sentient beings— To all these sublime Dharmas, I pay homage and praise.
The twelve teachings that are the natural outflow of the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), Primordially free from arising and ceasing, transcending conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*),
And through which the recollection of all merits is accomplished— I praise and pay homage to the seed of goodness,
the wondrous Dharma. To the Great Sun King (*Mahāvairocana*), who removes both folly and wisdom, The supreme physician who dispels the suffering of saṃsāra.
The King of Ambrosia who purifies all suffering and affliction;

To all the various sublime waters of the devas and other offerings for the sake of all the wondrous Dharmas, I dedicate [the merit] so that sentient beings may attain the bliss of the Buddha-way. Those who wish to extensively perform this should praise the Mother of Buddhas Prajñāpāramitā, the Savior Mother, and others, And uphold the teachings of the Sūtra, Vinaya, and Abhidharma Piṭakas, Holding in hand the alms bowl, the mendicant’s staff, and other such implements.
I serve the Teacher, the Supreme among all Dharmas, and make offerings to the assembly of noble Śrāvakas;

Like a sword of wisdom with a great and sharp blade, they personally realize the nature of all dependent origination and can manifest various supernatural transformations. I make offerings to the assembly of noble Pratyekabuddhas.
All the various sublime celestial waters and so forth are dedicated to sentient beings and the path of the Buddha.
To all the perfectly awakened ones of the three times, whose nature is the body of true wisdom,
whose countenances are wondrous, and who possess mastery over speech— to Mañjuśrī, I pay homage and offer praise.
With a pure mind, far removed from all defilements, you are adorned with the stainless light of merit;

humans and devas prostrate at your lotus feet. All the various sublime celestial waters and other offerings made to the Great Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī are dedicated to sentient beings and the path of the Buddhas.
Deliverer from the suffering of all sentient beings, Who releases them from the fetters of the three realms of existence,
And guides them upon the path of supreme liberation— To the Bodhisattva Deliverer, I pay homage!
To the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Deliverer, Whose body is red and who sits upon a lotus throne.
Holding the treasury of the sublime Dharma in the right hand, one makes offerings with the left fist pressed against the hip;
all the various sublime celestial waters and other offerings are dedicated to sentient beings and the path of the Buddha.
I pay homage and praise the Vajra-holder, the Great Lord of Light who subdues all māras through the secrets of body, speech, and mind,
who upholds the three times and the perfectly awakened ones, and who maintains the entire treasury of all sublime dharmas.
The assembly of the retinue of the Secret King, with reverence, makes offerings, praises, and prostrates;
all the various sublime celestial waters and so forth are dedicated to sentient beings and the path of the Buddha.
Possessing great compassion and the power of supernatural faculties, you are mindful and able to deliver others from all suffering and hardship;
like the bright sun, you illuminate all sentient beings.
To the All-Illuminating Honored One, I pay homage and offer various kinds of celestial and wondrous waters, dedicating these merits to all sentient beings and the path of the Buddha.
The Great Bodhisattva Candraprabha-kīrti-virocana, his body white, seated upon a lotus throne,
with two arms in the gesture of preaching the Dharma and holding a rosary;
may all offerings of various celestial and wondrous waters be respectfully presented, praised, and honored, and dedicated to sentient beings and the path of the Buddhas.
The Lord of Devas, Śakra, wielder of the thunderbolt; the various heavenly kings and lords of the māra hosts;
the assembly of deities belonging to the eastern quarter—homage and praise to you who are worshipped with offerings.
The Fire-Consumer, the deity of the fire sacrifice; the Great Sage, the king of spirits, and lord of the māra hosts.
To the assembly of immortals and their retinues in the southeast, I offer, praise, and prostrate.
To the Māra-king Jvalanaprabha who wields the jeweled staff, To the Śmaśānī goddesses, the divine kings, and the lords of the māra hosts,
And to the assembly of Yama’s followers in the south, I offer, praise, and prostrate.
The Yakṣa King, Lord of the Māra division, who dwells in the southwest with his retinue of yakṣas, who is far removed from worldly truths, possesses sublime divinity, and is honored,
praised, and venerated— homage to him! The Water Deity who wields the noose, the Nāga King, Lord of the Māra division.
To the assembly of the Western Dragon King’s retinue, I offer worship, praise, and prostration;

To the Wind Deity who Sustains Life, I offer worship, praise, and prostration; To the Lord of the Seed-Holding Spirits and the Sovereign of the Māra Division, And to the assembly of the Northwestern Wind King’s retinue, I offer worship, praise, and prostration.
Rākṣasa deity who wields the precious staff, guardian of the treasure-store, lord of the māra division,
and host of northern rākṣasas— to you we offer worship,
praise, and prostration. O Sovereign Lord, the Alluring Deity, King Vināyaka, lord of the māra division.
To the hosts of lords and their retinues in the northeast, I offer worship, praise, and prostration.
To all the celestial assemblies in the zenith— the deities of the sun, the moon, the planets, the constellations,
and their various divine retinues— I offer worship, praise, and prostration.
The Nāga King below, the Earth-Ruling Goddess,
And the retinue of Mahāhasta who guard the samaya— I offer worship, praise, and prostrate to you,
Who subdue all afflictions and possess great merit, The Honored Sattva who protects and saves the world.
Wondrous as a true jewel, embodiment of liberation, I present all manner of incomparable offerings, Including various kinds of argha water And the waters of worldly merit.
To you, the guardians of the ten directions, I make this offering; For the benefit of the noble patrons, I pray that you descend.
All varieties of celestial, wondrous flowers and so forth are dedicated to sentient beings and the Buddha-way.
Having severed the defilements of the mire of the desire realm, he dwells in the position of Brahmā, King of the Form Realm;
as Mahābrahmā, Lord of the Sahā World, he makes offerings to the assembly of Mahābrahmā’s retinue.
Three-faced and six-armed, subduer of asuras, Pervading all with the radiance of the nature of equality,
possessing great divine power in the celestial realms; I pay homage to Mahādeva Nārāyaṇa,
supreme among the gods of the higher worlds, And behold face-to-face Maitreya, the Honored One who provides protection.
Together with the devas of Tuṣita, the holy patrons reverently offer worship;
The Lord of the Asuras, who observes the three times with his three eyes, Protects the fourfold assembly of the Buddha’s teachings;
We pay homage to the Honored Śakra, Lord of Devas.
Dwelling before Śakra on Mount Sumeru, you follow skillful means to assist in the governance and transformation of all the celestial retinues.
O Holy Patron, may your offerings be perfected;
may you possess great, pure, and true faith, and utterly destroy the mountain of arrogance and self-conceit.
Attendants follow the Master’s instructions, making offerings to the assembly of the eight classes of spirits;
all these various sublime celestial waters and other substances are dedicated toward sentient beings and the path of the Buddha.
The Great Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra of the East, his body white in color, holding a lute, protects the eastern gate of the eight Buddhas;
he makes offerings and offers praise with reverence.
The offerings and so forth are the same as before, up to the dedication for sentient beings and the path of the Buddha.
The Great Heavenly King Virūḍhaka of the South, his body blue in color, holding a precious sword, protects the southern gate of the eight Buddhas. I make offerings, praise, and pay homage;
these offerings are the same as those previously described, dedicated to sentient beings and the path of the Buddhas.
The Great Heavenly King Virūpākṣa of the West, his body red in color and holding a noose, protects the western gate of the eight Buddhas. I make offerings, praise, and pay homage to him;
these offerings are as described previously, extending through the dedication for the sake of sentient beings and the path of the Buddhas.
The Great Heavenly King Vaishravana of the North, his body green in color, holding a jeweled trident, protects the northern gate of the eight Buddhas. I make offerings, praise, and pay homage;
these offerings are as described previously, up to the dedication for the sake of sentient beings and the path of the Buddhas.
The yakṣa kings, Piṅgala and the rest, each leading a retinue of seven hundred million,
have vowed to protect the teaching of the Tathāgata. I prostrate to all the great yakṣa kings,
the upāsakas of great majesty and power— the great yakṣa generals, Piṅgala and the others.
His body is yellow in color and he grasps a precious vajra; he leads a host of seven hundred million yakṣas and has vowed to protect the teachings of the Tathāgata.
To this upāsaka of great majesty and power, the Great Yakṣa General Pāñcika, we offer worship, praise, and prostrations.
His body is white in color and he wields a precious sword; He leads a host of seven hundred million yakṣas, vowing to protect the teachings of the Tathāgata.
I now respectfully offer worship to this upāsaka of great majestic power, The Great Yakṣa General Makhādeva (Mekhila).
His body is yellow in color and he wields a precious staff; He leads a host of seven hundred million yakṣas and has vowed to protect the Tathāgata’s teaching.
I now reverently offer worship to this upāsaka of great majestic power, The yakṣa general Andhira.
His body is green and he wields a precious mallet; He leads a host of seven hundred million yakṣas, Vowing to protect the teachings of the Tathāgata.
I now reverently offer worship to this upāsaka of great majesty and power, The yakṣa general Aṇila.
His body is red in color and he wields a jeweled trident; He leads a host of seven hundred million yakṣas and has vowed to protect the Tathāgata’s teaching.
I now respectfully present offerings to this upāsaka of great majestic power, The Great Yakṣa General Sandhira.
His body is smoke-colored and he wields a precious sword; He leads a host of seven hundred million yakṣas, having vowed to protect the Tathāgata’s teaching.
I now reverently offer worship to this upāsaka of great majestic power, The yakṣa general Indra.
His body is red in color and he wields a precious staff; He leads a host of seven hundred million yakṣas and vows to protect the teachings of the Tathāgata.
I now respectfully offer worship to this upāsaka of great majestic power, The great yakṣa general Pīla.
His body is crimson in color and he wields a precious mallet; He presides over a host of seven hundred million yakṣas, Vowing to protect the teachings of the Tathāgata.
I now reverently offer worship to this upāsaka of great majestic power, The yakṣa general Mahura.
His body is white in color and he wields a precious axe; He leads a host of seven hundred million yakṣas, Vowing to protect the teachings of the Tathāgata.
I now respectfully offer worship to this upāsaka of great majestic power, The yakṣa general Candana.
His body is yellow in color and he holds a noose; He leads a host of seven hundred million yakṣas, Vowing to protect the teachings of the Tathāgata.
I now respectfully offer worship to this upāsaka of great majestic power, The Great General of Yakṣas, Jālavāhana.
His body is blue in color and he wields a precious mallet; He presides over a host of seven hundred million yakṣas, Having vowed to protect the teachings of the Tathāgata.
I now respectfully offer worship to this upāsaka of great majestic power, The Great Yakṣa General Vajrapāṇi (Vikara).
His body is red in color and he holds a precious wheel; as the leader of seven hundred million yakṣas, he has vowed to protect the teachings of the Tathāgata.
I now respectfully present these various kinds of sublime celestial waters and other offerings; may they be dedicated to all sentient beings and to the path of the Buddha.
Until I have realized unsurpassed bodhi, may my body and life within the three realms arise solely through karma;
even if I must endure all manner of obstacles, I vow never to abandon the bodhicitta,
and only then shall I release this offering of food.
Next, perform the ritual bathing.
Afterwards, form the mudrā of returning home to repay the debt of gratitude,
and further offer this praise:
To the Teacher of Excellent Renown and Auspiciousness, whose body is yellow and who bears no mudrā,
seated upon the lion throne of the eight great supreme aspirations— I now make offerings, praise, and prostrate to this Teacher.
To the Buddha Ratnacandraprajñābhūṣaṇa, whose body is yellow and who displays the mudrā of sublime giving.
Upon the lion throne of the eight great supreme vows, I now make offerings, praise, and pay homage to the Guide,
the Buddha Golden Jewel Light (*Suvarṇaprabhāsa*), whose body is yellow and who is in the mudrā of preaching the Dharma.
Upon the lion throne of the four great supreme vows, I now make offerings, praise, and pay homage.
To the Teacher, the most supreme Buddha Aśoka, whose body is red and who sits upon a lion throne of the four great elements and the seal of samādhi;
I now offer worship, praise, and prostration to this Teacher.
To the Buddha Dharmasāgaragarjitasvara, whose body is white and who displays the seal of teaching the Dharma.
Upon a lion throne of the four great vows, I now offer worship, praise,
and prostration to the Sugata Dharmasāgaravijaya-jñāna, whose body is blue and who displays the mudrā of preaching the Dharma.
Upon a lion throne of the four great vows, I now offer worship, praise, and prostration.
Buddha Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabharāja, his body blue in color,
bestowing the seal of the twelve supreme vows upon the lion throne— now I make offerings, praise, and pay homage to this Guide,
the Honored Śākyasiṃha, his body yellow in color, in the mudrā of preaching the Dharma.
Upon the lion throne of the Great Vow, I now offer worship, praise, and prostration.
From countless eons in the past, out of compassion for all suffering sentient beings and for the sake of my ultimate,
subtle, and vast vow, I worship the eight honored Tathāgatas.
In times past, countless eons ago, you made subtle and supreme vows;
now, for the sake of fulfilling those pledges, you make offerings to the eight great Tathāgatas.
Your holy teaching is as vast as space; it is the ultimate truth, without objective referent, transcending all conceptual proliferation.
To the one whose perfect voice and wondrous marks are the nature of universal knowledge, Who makes offerings to Prajñāpāramitā, the Mother of all Buddhas,
Whose unbeginning habitual tendencies are the empty intrinsic nature, Who can expound the various dharmas of the emptiness of nature,
And who manifests the form of a youth as the principle of reality— To Mañjuśrī of Great Wisdom, I pay homage and praise.

Protector who rescues from the suffering of the six realms and eight difficulties, Who delivers beings across the sea of misery to the other shore and leads them into Nirvana— To that Great Teacher, Bodhisattva Jie-duo (Guhyapāda), I pay homage.
Your adamantine jewel-body is immovable; You are the King of the Power of Secret Mantra and Great Wisdom.
I pay homage to the Vajrapāṇi Bhagavān, the Lord of Sugatas who has realized perfect awakening; To him who can discipline all sentient beings difficult to tame,
who is the sovereign of the ten stages, the Dharma King,
or who manifests as a youth to benefit sentient beings— I make offerings to him in such infinite ways.
Bhagavān Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha, Holder of the most supreme and wondrous Dharma-treasury,
Bringing benefit and joy to sentient beings like the sun and moon, I pay homage and praise the one of supreme radiance;
I take refuge in and honor the teachings of the Sūtra, Vinaya, and Abhidharma collections, And those who hold the alms bowl, mendicant’s staff, and other emblems.
I serve the Teacher, the Supreme among all Dharmas, And make offerings to the assembly of noble Śrāvakas.
In the east is Śakra, Lord of the Hundred Sacrifices;
His body is yellow, he holds a precious vajra, And he sits upon a white elephant throne. I now make offerings, praise, and pay homage to him.
In the southeast is the Fire God, the Great Brahmā Rishi;
his body is red in color, he holds a *kamaṇḍalu*, and he sits upon a red goat throne. I now make offerings, praise, and pay homage to the Southern Queen, Yamadūtī;
her body is blue in color, and she holds a precious staff.
Riding upon a blue water buffalo, I now offer worship, praise, and prostration to the Yakṣa King of the Southwestern Direction, Vidhura.
His body is black, he wields a precious sword, and he rides a powerful vetāla;
I now offer worship, praise, and prostration.
In the west is Varuṇa, the water deity; his body is white, he holds a snake-noose, and he sits upon a nāga-water creature. I now make offerings to him, praise him, and pay homage.
To the northwest is Vāyu, the wind deity; his body is smoke-colored, and he holds a multicolored banner.
Riding upon a great green deer, I now offer, praise, and prostrate to Kuvera, the Lord of the North who bestows wealth.
His body is yellow in color, he holds a pouch of mice, and he sits upon a throne of a blue horse-king; I now offer, praise, and prostrate to him.
In the northeast is the Lord Māra-rāja; his body is white, he holds a jeweled trident, and he sits upon a throne of a blue bull-king.
Now I make offerings to, praise, and pay homage to all the hosts of devas in the zenith:
the Sun Deva, the Moon Deva, and the Devas who hold the celestial bodies.
To the host of constellations and their celestial retinues, I offer, praise, and pay homage.
To the Dragon Kings of the lower regions and the Earth-protecting Deities, who uphold the great earth with their mighty hands,
and to their retinues who guard the samaya, I offer, praise, and pay homage.
Upāsaka who protects the Buddha’s teachings, manifesting bodies through skillful means according to the capacities of beings;
yakṣa generals such as Piṅgala and others, along with a great host of yakṣas,
praise and pay homage to this auspicious upāsaka of majestic power, who is fierce, violent, and most formidable.
To Kuṇḍalin and Cakravartin, to Vikarāla and the others, I make offerings.

Whatever merit there is from all acts of worship, praise, and offering; by requesting the Buddhas to remain in the world and turn the wheel of Dharma, and by rejoicing in and repenting for all roots of goodness—may this be dedicated so that all beings may attain the path to Buddhahood.
Because of my ignorance and lack of knowledge, The virtuous deeds I have cultivated have been inconsistent;
Now, for the sake of protecting all sentient beings, I pray that the Venerable One will grant me patience and acceptance.
I have not yet fully realized the sublime power of the Sovereign Lord, And thus whatever is incomplete or deficient in my practice, Or whatever is dull and inferior, [may it be forgiven].
Should there be any transgressions against such [teachings], we pray that the Venerable One will graciously forgive them.
Having already brought benefit to us sentient beings, please grant the fulfillment of our aspirations.
We respectfully escort the World-Honored One back to his own land; we pray that you will look upon us with compassion and descend once more.
The Ritual Manual for Recitation and the Method of Offering for the *Sūtra on the Merit of the Fundamental Vows of the Seven Buddhas, the King Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha*
